claim: The newest JUCE tag found by ls-remote is 9.0.5 (highest of 9.0.0-9.0.5), so the current major version is JUCE 9; its LICENSE.md says the framework modules are dual-licensed under AGPLv3 or the commercial JUCE licence (JUCE 9 EULA).

JUCE's own SPDX bill of materials declares JUCE 9.0.5 and every juce_* module as 'AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-JUCE-Commercial', so an AGPL-3.0-only project using the open-source option is within the declared terms; examples are ISC-licensed per LICENSE.md lines 51-53.

Under the JUCE 9 EULA route (not AGPL) the user agrees to the EULA at juce.com/legal/juce-9-licence by merely downloading, installing, using or combining JUCE with other code; the AGPL route is stated as an alternative ('Or: You may also use this code under the terms of the AGPLv3') in each module header.

AGPLv3 section 5(c) requires that a modified/combined work be licensed as a whole under the AGPL to everyone receiving a copy; combined with JUCE's AGPL option, a distributed JUCE-based plug-in therefore has to be offered under AGPLv3 as a whole (deduced from AGPL 5(c) plus JUCE's dual licence; JUCE's own text does not restate it, and I did not read the EULA page, which was blocked).

JUCE 9.0.5 contains no splash screen: juce_gui_basics.cpp emits a compiler warning that JUCE_DISPLAY_SPLASH_SCREEN and JUCE_USE_DARK_SPLASH_SCREEN are ignored, so no splash-screen obligation exists in the build at that tag, whichever licence is chosen.

A JUCE staff post dated 2026-06-17 states that JUCE 9 keeps the same licence tiers and prices as JUCE 8 and that the JUCE 9 EULA is unchanged from the final JUCE 8 EULA; the post does not mention the AGPL.

JUCE 9.0.5 vendors the VST3 SDK at version 3.8.0 under MIT, in modules/juce_audio_processors_headless/format_types/VST3_SDK; the vendored LICENSE.txt is MIT, copyright 2025 Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH.

JUCE 9.0.5's SPDX inventory lists other bundled third-party code: zlib 1.3.2 (Zlib), HarfBuzz 15.0.0 (MIT-Modern-Variant), libpng 1.6.58 (libpng-2.0), jpeglib 10.0 (IJG), FLAC 1.5.0, libogg 1.3.6, libvorbis 1.3.7 (all BSD-3-Clause), Oboe 1.10.0 (Apache-2.0), Box2D 2.2.1 (Zlib), ASIO SDK 2.3 (Steinberg ASIO licence OR GPL-3.0-only); all are permissive or GPL-compatible, and attribution notices must be carried when binaries are redistributed.

The VST3 SDK at tag v3.8.1_build_84 is licensed under the MIT licence (copyright 2026 Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH); the SDK README states that GPLv3 and the Steinberg proprietary licence are no longer available.

Steinberg's SDK README says use of the VST name or VST Compatible logo is optional under MIT, but if used it must follow Steinberg's rules: unaltered logo, only in clear product contexts (splash screens, about boxes, websites, documentation); 'VST' (or VSTi etc.) must not be used in company or product names; the logo must not go on non-VST-compatible products.

The Steinberg VST Usage Guidelines (dev-portal page) require, when the VST name or logo is used, the statement 'VST is a registered trademark of Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH' with the (R) on first use (section 15), forbid 'VST' in company names (s7) and logos (s10), forbid derivatives such as 'VSTi' (s13), forbid stylising VST or merging it into a product brand (s6), and allow plain-text 'for VST' beside the logo in product names (s6). Note the README says 'VST trademark'; the guidelines page says 'registered trademark'.

claim: The cheapest compliant approach for a hobby plug-in is to avoid 'VST' in product names and file names (e.g. use 'VST3' only descriptively as a format in documentation, with the attribution sentence) and not display the logo; the README makes the logo optional. This is my deduction from the cited rules, not a Steinberg statement.

Rack v2.6.6 LICENSE.md: Rack's code is GPL v3 'or any later version', plus the 'VCV Rack Non-Commercial Plugin License Exception' under GPLv3 section 7: a Plugin (a library linked and executed by Rack) may use Rack's API and link to it regardless of the Plugin's own licence terms, provided the Plugin is distributed free of charge.

Rack's LICENSE.md says non-commercial plug-ins need not be GPLv3 and may use any licence (open-source or proprietary freeware), but plug-ins that copy a significant portion of non-API Rack source must be GPLv3.

The VCV manual's Plugin Licensing page recommends GPL-3.0-or-later for free open-source plug-ins and lists MIT/BSD/CC0 or closed freeware as allowed under the exception, provided the plug-in is free of charge; donationware only if a donation is not required.

claim: The Rack Component Library graphics are copyright VCV 2016-2023 under CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial use with credit; commercial use only via VCV Library or commercial licence); the visual design of Core modules is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (no derivatives); the VCV logo/icon may not be used in derivative works; the 'VCV' name may not be used for unofficial products but 'for VCV Rack' is acceptable.

CC BY-NC graphics are not compatible with an AGPL-3.0-only repository (the NC restriction is an additional restriction), so Component Library SVGs must not be copied into the repository; the project plans its own panel design. claim: The VCV Plugin Ethics Guidelines say not to copy the brand name, model name, logo, panel design or component layout (knobs, ports, switches) of an existing hardware or software product without the owner's permission, whether or not trademark or copyright law covers them; they are recommended for all plug-ins but mandatory for the VCV Library and for commercial licences.

Consequence: a faithful Moogerfooger clone with the Moog/Moogerfooger names or a copy of Moog's panel/layout could not be submitted to the VCV Library, but a self-distributed free plug-in is only 'recommended' to follow the ethics rules. Deduced from the two preceding claims.

GPLv3 section 13 grants permission to link or combine any GPLv3-covered work with an AGPLv3 work into one combined work; the GPL terms continue to apply to the GPL part and AGPL section 13 network terms apply to the combination.
AGPLv3 section 13 (second paragraph) gives the reciprocal permission to combine an AGPL-covered work with a GPLv3 work; the GPL-covered part remains under GPLv3.

Rack is GPL-3.0-or-later (version 3 or any later version at the licensee's option), so the version-3 option exists for combining with an AGPL-3.0-only project, and the plug-in exception additionally lets a free plug-in carry any licence, so an AGPL-3.0-only Rack plug-in is permitted either way.

MIT (VST3 SDK, JUCE-bundled) and BSL-1.0 (Catch2 devel branch LICENSE.txt, Catch2 CMake version 3.16.1) are permissive licences whose texts impose only notice retention (BSL-1.0 exempts machine-executable object code) and contain no copyleft; that they are one-way compatible with AGPL-3.0 is FSF's published view, which I did not read (www.gnu.org blocked), so this is inferred.

The AGPL-3.0-only repository must use the same mechanism Rack and JUCE rely on: whoever receives binaries must be offered corresponding source; a dual-use design (VST3 via JUCE under AGPL; Rack plug-in under AGPL via GPL section 13 or the plug-in exception) needs source for both on the public repository.
